transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

For weeks I’ve had this nonstop drive to take on more at the hospital, like I can’t slow my mind or body down even when I know it’s too much. It's gotten to the point where I just really need some help figuring out what's going on.
During this time, have you had any hallucinations, or felt unusually certain that you had special powers, a special mission, or that others were trying to harm or control you?

Yeah, during that high phase, I kept hearing a calm male voice telling me I was "chosen to fix the system" and that the patients depended on me. I was also completely convinced the hospital was secretly grooming me to lead a new program to overhaul patient care. Those things only happened when I was super wired, though, and they completely stopped once I crashed.

Have you ever had a similar episode of feeling abnormally energized, needing much less sleep, talking more, or becoming overly confident before this one, or is this the first time it has ever happened?

No, this is the very first time I've ever felt like this. It all started about two months ago when I began juggling my first job, night shifts, and studying for my CNA exam. Before this, everyone knew me as a really calm and methodical person.
Have you started, stopped, or changed any medications or used any substances such as stimulants, antidepressants, steroids, cocaine, or energy drinks around the time this began?

No, I haven't started or stopped any medications, and I don't use any drugs like cocaine or steroids. The only thing is that I relied really heavily on coffee to get through those long shifts when I was feeling so wired.
Besides coffee, have you used any stimulants or other substances around the time this started, such as ADHD medications, cocaine, methamphetamine, or diet pills?
No, I’ve never taken any ADHD medications, diet pills, or street drugs like that. It really was just a lot of coffee to keep me going during those shifts. I've never used anything else.
Did the symptoms start only after you began using a lot of coffee or any other stimulant, and did they improve when you cut back or stopped it?

I actually only drank that much coffee to get through the long night shifts when I was already feeling really wired, so I'm not sure if it caused the symptoms. Plus, cutting back on coffee hasn't helped at all with this heavy, low feeling I have now.

Did the very high energy, decreased need for sleep, and hearing the voice ever happen only when you had a lot of caffeine or any other stimulant, and did they go away within a day or two after stopping it?

No, those symptoms actually lasted continuously for weeks at a time, and they didn't just go away in a day or two when I stopped drinking coffee. I only drank the coffee during my shifts because I was too busy and wired to eat, but the high energy, lack of sleep, and the voice persisted through that entire high phase before I finally crashed.

How long did the high-energy, decreased-sleep, and voice-hearing symptoms continue after you stopped or cut back on coffee? Did they fully go away within a day or two, or did they last for weeks even without caffeine?

I'm not really sure about that, and I haven't thought much about the connection between the coffee and how long those symptoms lasted. I just know that the intense energy and the voice seemed to keep going for weeks on their own regardless of what I was drinking.
Did the high energy, decreased need for sleep, and hearing the voice start only after you began drinking a lot of coffee, and did they go away within a day or two after you stopped or cut back?

No, the coffee didn't cause it; I actually only started drinking it because I was already so wired and busy that I was skipping meals. Those symptoms lasted for weeks on end and didn't go away in a day or two when I cut back on caffeine. They only finally stopped when I crashed into this heavy, low phase about a month ago.

Before this episode, had you ever had any periods of several days to weeks of unusually high energy, less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or feeling overly confident without using caffeine or any other substance?

No, I have never had any episodes like this before, as I am normally a very calm and methodical person. This entire cycle only started about two months ago when I began juggling night shifts and studying for my CNA exam. It definitely wasn't caused by any substances, though I did drink coffee back then when I forgot to eat.
Since the high-energy period ended, have you had any time when your mood and energy were completely back to normal for at least a couple of weeks, or have you stayed depressed the whole time?

No, I haven't had any periods where I felt back to normal. Since I crashed about a month ago, I've stayed depressed and completely drained the entire time. It's just been this constant, heavy low every single day without any break.
When you were in the high-energy phase, did it begin only after you started drinking a lot of coffee or any other stimulant, and did it go away within a day or two after you stopped?

No, the coffee didn't start it at all; I only drank it because I was already so wired and busy that I was skipping meals. That high state didn't go away in a day or two when I stopped, but instead lasted for several weeks until I finally crashed into this exhausted phase.
Did your high-energy episode start only after you began drinking a lot of coffee, and did it go away within a day or two after you stopped or cut back?

No, the high energy didn't start from the coffee; I actually only drank it because I was already so wired and busy that I forgot to eat. That high phase lasted for weeks rather than just a day or two, and it only ended when I crashed into this low phase about a month ago.
Did the high-energy episode begin only after you started drinking a lot of coffee or any other stimulant, and did it go away within a day or two after you stopped or cut back?

Like I mentioned, the coffee didn't start any of this; I only drank it because I was already too wired to sit down and eat. That high state lasted for weeks on end and didn't go away when I stopped drinking coffee. It only stopped when I crashed into this heavy, depressed phase that has been dragging on for almost a month now.
Did your high-energy symptoms and hearing the voice start only after you began using a lot of coffee or another stimulant, and did they go away within a day or two after you stopped or cut back?

No, the high energy and the voice definitely didn't start because of the coffee; I only drank it because I was already so wired and busy that I was skipping meals. Those symptoms lasted for weeks and didn't just go away in a day or two when I stopped drinking it. They only stopped when I crashed into this heavy, low phase that has been dragging on for nearly a month now.

Did your high-energy, decreased-sleep, and voice-hearing symptoms start only after you began using a stimulant or a lot of caffeine, and did they go away within a day or two after you stopped or cut back?

No, the coffee didn't cause any of it; I only drank it because I was already so wired and busy that I was skipping meals. Those symptoms lasted for weeks and didn't go away when I cut back on caffeine. They only stopped when I crashed into this heavy, low phase that I've been stuck in for about a month now.
Did the high-energy episode and hearing the voice happen only while you were using a stimulant or a lot of caffeine, and did they stop within a day or two after you cut back or stopped?

No, those symptoms didn't only happen while I was drinking coffee, and I have never used any other stimulants. The intense energy and the voice lasted continuously for weeks and didn't go away within a day or two of stopping. Instead, they only stopped when I crashed into this heavy low phase that has been dragging on for nearly a month now.
Have you ever had any similar high-energy, decreased-sleep, or hearing-voices episodes when you were not using caffeine or any other substance, even if it was years ago?

No, this is the very first time in my life I've ever experienced these high-energy phases, low sleep, or heard voices, and it all started about two months ago when I began juggling my new job and exam prep. While I did drink a lot of coffee to get through shifts during that high phase, I have never had any episodes like this in the past or years ago.

Did the high-energy and voice-hearing symptoms begin only after you started drinking a lot of coffee, or did they clearly start before the coffee and keep going even when you cut back? Did they stop within a day or two of reducing caffeine, or did they last for weeks on their own?

The high energy and the voice definitely started before the coffee; I only drank it because I was already so wired and too busy to eat actual meals. They didn't stop when I cut back on caffeine either, but lasted for weeks on their own during that whole high period.
How long did the high-energy phase last in total, and did it continue for at least one week with very little need for sleep and feeling unusually energized or irritable?

Yes, that high-energy phase lasted for about a month in total before I crashed. During those weeks, I was getting only three or four hours of sleep a night but still felt incredibly wired, and I would get really snappy and irritated if anyone tried to slow me down.
Have you ever had any previous episodes of depression, or any earlier periods of unusually high energy, less need for sleep, or feeling overly confident before this one?

No, I've never had any episodes of depression or high energy before this. My life was completely normal before, and these symptoms only started about two months ago when I began juggling my new job and the CNA exam prep. This is the very first time I've ever experienced these extreme highs or heavy lows.
Have you ever had any previous episodes of depression, or any earlier periods of unusually high energy, less need for sleep, or feeling overly confident before this one?

Like I said, this is the very first time I have ever experienced anything like this. Before starting my job and finishing high school about two months ago, I was always my usual calm, methodical self. I've never had any previous episodes of depression or these intense high-energy phases before.
During the high-energy period, did these symptoms last for at least one week and cause major problems at work, school, or with relationships?

Yes, the high-energy phase lasted for several weeks and caused huge disruptions in my life. I ended up getting written up at work, missing multiple shifts and classes, and falling way behind on my CNA exam prep. I also completely stopped hanging out with my friends because I was either too wound up or too exhausted to socialize.
During this depressed period, have you had any thoughts of death or suicide, or felt that life is not worth living?

Lately, I do feel like there's no point in trying and that everyone would be better off if I had never gotten this job. But even though I feel like a huge burden, I don't have any active thoughts of wanting to end my life or suicide.
During this depressed period, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or had changes in sleep, appetite, concentration, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness?

Since I crashed, I've barely had an appetite and have dropped a bunch of weight, and even though I sleep in late, I keep waking up at night and never feel rested. I also just feel this heavy, constant guilt, like I've let down my parents, coworkers, and patients so badly that they'd all be better off if I hadn't gotten this job in the first place.
During this depressed period, have you had any hallucinations or strong false beliefs, like hearing voices, feeling specially chosen, or believing people are trying to harm or control you?

No, those experiences only happened during that super wired stretch when I was barely sleeping. Since I crashed into this low, depressed phase, the voice and the belief that I was chosen to fix the system have completely stopped.
During this depressed period, have you had any hallucinations or strong false beliefs, like hearing voices, feeling specially chosen, or believing people are trying to harm or control you?

No, those experiences only happened during that high, wired phase when I was barely sleeping. Since I crashed into this depressed period, those voices and beliefs have completely stopped and I haven't had them at all. It's just been this heavy, empty feeling lately.
Have you ever had any past episodes of feeling unusually high, energized, needing much less sleep, or becoming more talkative or impulsive before this illness started?

No, I have never experienced anything like this before in my life. These highs and lows are completely new to me and only started about two months ago when I began juggling my first job, night shifts, and studying for my CNA exam.
During this depressed period, have you had any hallucinations or strong false beliefs, like hearing voices or feeling specially chosen, even when you were not feeling energized or barely sleeping?

No, I haven't had any of those experiences during this depressed phase. Hearing the voice and believing I was specially chosen only happened during that high, wired stretch when I wasn't sleeping. Since I crashed, those things have completely stopped and I haven't experienced them at all.
Since you became depressed, have you still had any periods of unusually high energy, needing much less sleep, racing thoughts, or feeling unusually confident, even for a day or two?

No, I haven't had any of those high-energy or confident periods at all since I crashed. For the past month, it has just been a continuous, heavy, and completely exhausted state every single day. I haven't had even a day or two of feeling wired or sleeping less.
